chunks: Al-Sakuni narrated through his chain of transmission that Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said:

Regarding a man who ordered his slave to kill a man and he killed him, he said: “Is the slave of a man anything but like his whip and his sword?” So the master was executed, and the slave was committed to prison.

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali عليه السلام
key_terms.اسْتُودِعَ الْعَبْدُ السِّجْنَ: the slave was placed in prison
key_terms.سَيْفِهِ: his sword, meaning a tool used by the master
key_terms.كَسَوْطِهِ: like his whip, meaning an instrument under his command

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man orders his slave to kill someone and the slave carries it out?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a master who commands his slave to commit murder. Imam Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام assigns principal liability to the master, treating the slave as an instrument in carrying out the crime, so the master is executed and the slave is imprisoned.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3262 - Al-Sakuni narrated through his chain of transmission that Commander of the Faithful (as) said

regarding a man who ordered his slave to kill another man, and the slave carried out the order:
(Imam (as) said) "Is not the slave like his master's whip or sword?"
Therefore, the master was executed, and the slave was imprisoned.
